rationales: Butter is a liquid dispersed in a solid, so it is a liquid-in-solid solution.
Fog consists of liquid droplets dispersed in a gas.
Salt in water is a solid-in-liquid solution.
Sugar in water is a solid-in-liquid solution.
A triple covalent bond contains three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Eight electrons would be four shared pairs, not a triple bond.
Four electrons make two shared pairs, which is a double bond.
Three electrons cannot form a triple covalent bond, which has six shared electrons.
Covalent bonding generally involves sharing electrons rather than transfer between an electropositive and electronegative element.
Polar covalent bonding is unequal sharing, whereas such combinations typically transfer electrons.
An electropositive element can transfer electrons to an electronegative element, forming an ionic bond.
Coordinate covalent bonding involves a shared pair donated by one atom, not the usual bond in this combination.
HCl is diatomic, so it is not polyatomic.
CH₄ has five atoms per molecule and is polyatomic.
H₂ is diatomic, so it is not polyatomic.
CO₂ has three atoms per molecule and is polyatomic.
HCl is a molecular compound and is represented by molecules.
C₆H₆ is a molecular compound and is represented by molecules.
NaCl is an ionic compound represented by a formula unit.
H₂O is a molecular compound and is represented by molecules.
98 g is the molar mass of one mole, not the mass of one molecule.
One H₂SO₄ molecule has a molecular mass of 98 amu.
9.8 amu is too small; the molecular mass is 98 amu.
9.8 g is neither the molecular mass nor the molar mass of H₂SO₄.
An anion forms when an atom gains electrons.
Removing electrons from an atom does not produce a molecule.
An atom that loses electrons becomes a positively charged cation.
A molecular ion is a charged group of bonded atoms, not the usual result described here.
Light water is ordinary water, mainly containing protium.
Soft water has low concentrations of calcium and magnesium ions.
Hard water is defined by dissolved calcium or magnesium salts, not by deuterium.
Deuterium is used to make heavy water, D₂O.
Lattice energy concerns the formation of an ionic solid from gaseous ions.
Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron.
Electronegativity describes an atom’s attraction for shared electrons in a bond.
Electron affinity is the energy released when an atom gains an electron.
O₂ has a complete octet around each oxygen atom.
BF₃ is electron-deficient because boron has only six electrons around it in the molecule.
N₂ has a triple bond that gives each nitrogen an octet.
NH₃ has three bonds and a lone pair, giving nitrogen an octet.
Grams of solute per 100 g of solution is mass-by-mass percentage, % m/m.
% m/v expresses grams of solute per 100 mL of solution.
% v/m expresses volume of solute per mass of solution.
% v/v expresses volume of solute per volume of solution.
Benzene is nonpolar and is not the usual solvent for polar covalent compounds.
Ether is less polar than water and is not the expected solvent here.
Water is polar and commonly dissolves polar covalent compounds.
Petrol is nonpolar and generally dissolves nonpolar substances.
Coordinate covalent bonding involves a shared pair donated by one atom, not electron transfer.
Covalent bonding involves sharing electrons between atoms.
Metallic bonding involves delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
Electron transfer produces oppositely charged ions and results in ionic bonding.
Groups are the vertical columns of the periodic table.
Blocks are regions classified by the subshell being filled.
Periods are the horizontal rows of the periodic table.
Triads are historical groups of three elements, not the horizontal lines.
Both HCl and H₂O contain polar covalent bonds.
C₂H₂ is generally treated as having nonpolar or nearly nonpolar C–H bonds, while H₂O has polar covalent bonds.
N₂ has a nonpolar covalent bond, while H₂O has polar covalent bonds.
Cl₂ and O₂ each have nonpolar covalent bonds between identical atoms.
